page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 16 vCPUs and 64 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance is powered by an Intel processor with 8 physical cores and hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The CPU allocation is dedicated, ensuring consistent compute performance. The processor features a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, with hardware support for advanced instruction sets including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions and Advanced Vector Extensions.

Benchmark results place the n4-standard-16 in the average performance tier across most standardized tests. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1855.0 and a multi-core score of 11352.0. In memory performance, the instance records a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 1107.55 GB/sec, while uncached large block read and write speeds reach 117.6 GB/sec and 67.32 GB/sec, respectively. For specialized workloads, the instance demonstrates strong performance in text generation for small language models at 282.68 tokens/sec, though larger 7B model text generation operates at an average rate of 12.18 tokens/sec.

This instance does not include bundled local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, meaning storage resources must be attached separately. Given its balanced resource distribution and average database operation benchmark of 7748.52, the n4-standard-16 is suited for general-purpose workloads, including web serving, software compilation, and moderate database operations. Its qualitative cost profile reflects a standard mid-tier resource density, offering a predictable balance of compute and memory without the premium overhead of specialized GPU or high-density storage hardware.
description: The Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-16 is an x86_64 general-purpose server instance configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 64 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel processor with 8 physical cores and hyper-threading, it features a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets like Intel AMX and AVX-512. The instance does not include bundled local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Performance benchmarks generally fall within the average tier, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 11352.0 and a static web serving throughput of 22.14 GB/sec. It demonstrates strong performance in small-model LLM text generation at 282.68 tokens/sec. This instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for balanced workloads, making it suitable for general-purpose applications, software compilation, web serving, and moderate database operations.
